title: Longitudinal Neck Stroking
summary: Both hands make parallel, smooth passes along the back of the neck without applying direct pressure to the spine.
goal: Gently relax superficial tissues and establish a calm rhythm before rubbing or kneading techniques.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of longitudinal stroking along the posterior neck with both hands.
startingPosition: The head is supported and the neck remains neutral. The hands rest on either side of the posterior midline.
instructions: Place both hands symmetrically beside the spine.
Glide along the neck in a longitudinal direction.
Maintain even speed and light pressure.
Avoid pressing directly over the spinous processes.
direction: Parallel longitudinal movements over the soft tissues along the back of the neck.
tips: Reduce pressure near the base of the skull.
mistakes: Uneven speed between the two hands.
Using deep pressure in the small neck area.
warning: The cervical region requires gentle work. Avoid deep pressure when pain, recent injury, or neurological symptoms are present.
telegramCaption: Parallel gentle passes along the posterior neck.
